title: Range Addition
statement: Start with a list of `length` zeros. Each update [start, end, inc] adds inc to every position from start to end inclusive (0-based). Return the list after all updates.

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(29)
    n = 100000
    ups = []
    for _ in range(100000):
        a = r.randint(0, n - 1)
        ups.append([a, r.randint(a, n - 1), r.randint(-50, 50)])
    return [n, ups]

hints.1_question: Adding inc to a whole range one cell at a time is slow. What if you only record where the increase starts and where it stops?
hints.2_nudge: Store +inc at start and -inc just after end in a helper array. A running sum over that array rebuilds the final values.
hints.3_big_hint: diff has length+1. diff[start] += inc; diff[end+1] -= inc. out[i] = running sum of diff[0..i].

known_bugs.name: difference array too short (fails when end is the last index)
known_bugs.followup: Where does the '-inc' marker go for a range that ends at the final index? Does your array have a slot for it?

known_bugs.name: cancels at end instead of end + 1
known_bugs.followup: The range includes `end`. At which index should the value stop being added?

known_bugs.name: applies every update cell by cell (O(n * m))
known_bugs.followup: How many cell updates happen if 100000 updates each cover tens of thousands of cells? How can two markers replace the loop?

followups: Why does a running sum recover the totals?
How is this the inverse of a prefix sum?
